rationale: Start with a broad scouting gradient at moderate temperature to elute all 8 compounds and map the overall elution window without risking truncation. This should reveal whether peaks are compressed early, late, or across the full range so later runs can tighten the window and adjust slope.

The peaks elute in a narrow window corresponding to roughly phi 0.20–0.44, so trim the gradient around that region to make it much shallower where the critical pair sits. Keeping tG and T fixed isolates the effect of narrowing the phi window on the unresolved 4/5 pair.

The narrow window helped the 4/5 pair but pushed the first peak too close to the void and created a new late critical pair; lowering phi0 should retain and spread the early/mid peaks while keeping the useful upper window. This tests whether the key issue is the lower bound placement rather than slope alone.

Run the fully resolved method with a shorter gradient to recover time while checking which pair first becomes limiting. Since all pairs have margin at tG 20, a modest step steeper should improve CRF if selectivity is robust.

At tG 16 the limiting issue is compressed late elution, especially pair 6/7, so lowering phi1 should shallow the upper part of the gradient and spread the late peaks without lengthening tG. This directly tests whether the weak pair is controlled by the high-phi end of the window.

The 16 min, 0.20–0.45 method is fully resolved with some margin, so shorten tG one step to trade a bit of resolution for faster analysis. This should show whether we can push CRF higher before either the 4/5 or 6/7 pair drops below 1.5.

Since shortening the slope hurts the same two pairs, test temperature as an orthogonal selectivity lever while keeping the best window and tG. A 5 C increase may preserve or improve the critical separations while pulling the last peak closer to 10 min and improving CRF.

At 45 C the new limiting pair moved into the middle of the chromatogram, suggesting the lower part of the gradient window now needs more room. Lowering phi0 should shallow the early-to-mid region and may recover the 3/4 separation while keeping the faster high-temperature run.

Lowering phi0 made the run too long and did not fix the 3/4 pair, so instead tighten the upper end to make the whole gradient shallower without extending the low-phi region. This may improve the mid-window 3/4 separation while also pulling the last peak down versus the 0.20–0.45, 40 C method.

At 45 C the limiting 3/4 pair appears largely insensitive to window changes, so test a slightly shallower slope by extending tG one step. This should show whether the pair responds to gradient steepness at all while only modestly increasing the time penalty.

The critical pair changes identity with temperature and is nearly insensitive to slope at 45 C, so move temperature the other direction from 40 C to probe selectivity. A 35 C run may preserve the fully resolved pattern while increasing retention enough to reveal whether a lower temperature can separate the pair better than 40–45 C.

Temperature clearly changes selectivity strongly, so continue upward from the current best 45 C to see if the 3/4 pair improves enough while the run gets shorter. This is the most promising orthogonal move for exceeding the current best CRF.

Temperature has a nonmonotonic effect on selectivity, with 35 C causing a 6/7 collapse and 50 C causing a 3/4 collapse, so map the remaining low-temperature point to bracket the optimum. This helps confirm whether 40 C is the true selectivity sweet spot or if another temperature family is worth exploiting.

The data indicate 40 C gives the best overall selectivity, while 0.20–0.50 at 20 min had full resolution with the best minimum R margin. Try a slightly shorter 18 min version to reduce the time penalty while staying shallower than the failed 16 min run.

The current best is near full credit but limited by one late pair, so test a small temperature increase on this stronger upper window to see if 6/7 improves without sacrificing too much time. This uses temperature as a fine selectivity adjustment around the new best method.

The best method is limited by an early-mid pair at 45 C, so lower phi0 to make the lower half of the gradient shallower while keeping the stronger upper end and the good run time. This targets the 3/4 pair specifically and tests whether extra low-phi space can lift it above 1.5 without excessive delay.

Lowering phi0 worsened the 3/4 pair, so move the lower bound upward instead to see if centering the gradient later improves the early-mid selectivity at 45 C while keeping the fast overall elution. This directly probes whether the best 45 C method wants a narrower, higher phi window.

The new best method has no time penalty and two pairs just below full credit, so the only route upward is a slightly shallower gradient. Extending tG one step should test whether both critical pairs gain enough resolution to offset the modest increase in t_last.

The only remaining deficit is pair 3/4 at R 1.36, and there is still a little room before the 10 min penalty begins. Lengthening to 22 min is the most direct test of whether that pair can cross 1.5 while staying essentially penalty-free.

The 3/4 pair barely responds to tG, so test a different phi window while keeping the successful early start and no time penalty. Raising phi1 may shift selectivity enough for the stubborn 3/4 pair while preserving fast elution of the late compounds.

Use the successful higher-start window at 40 C, where selectivity was generally better behaved, and make the gradient slightly shallower to protect the late pair. This probes whether 40 C can improve the stubborn 3/4 separation enough to outweigh a small time penalty.

The best region is clearly around 45 C with phi1 0.50, and the remaining weak pair is early-mid while the last peak still has margin under 10 min. Raising phi0 one step should concentrate the gradient later and may improve the stubborn 3/4 selectivity while likely keeping the run penalty-free.

With only a few injections left, keep the best window and test the remaining untried higher temperature on it, since temperature has been the main source of selectivity changes for the stubborn early-mid pair. This is the most plausible remaining orthogonal move that could push 3/4 above 1.5 while likely retaining a sub-10 min last peak.

The best method is very close, and lowering phi1 may slightly shallow the critical early-mid region while still likely keeping the last peak under 10 min from the strong 0.25 start. This is a focused window adjustment around the best method to try to lift the stubborn 3/4 pair without invoking a time penalty.

For the final shot, keep the best-performing window and slope and use the last untested temperature extreme as the only remaining orthogonal lever for the stubborn 3/4 pair. The best current method is already near-optimal, so this is a high-upside final attempt to change selectivity enough to reach full credit while likely staying under the time limit.
